features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddy Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
Tarik Skubal and the New York Mets are in agreement on a nine-year, $450 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
The New York Yankees and right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga are in agreement on a two-year deal with a club option for 2029, sources told ESPN, reuniting the reliever and club after a season apart.
Right-hander Troy Melton and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a six-year, $46.5 million contract extension, sources tell ESPN.
Outfielder Gavin Sheets and the San Diego Padres are in agreement on a three-year, $11 million contract, sources tell ESPN.

The Colorado Rockies are acquiring right-handers Davis Martin and Luis Castillo in a trade with the Chicago White Sox, sources tell ESPN. The White Sox are getting LHP Sean Sullivan and catching prospect Douglas Veliz in return.
Right-hander Randy Dobnak and the Kansas City Royals are in agreement on a one-year, $1.35 million contract, a source tells ESPN.

features.headline: What Tarik Skubal's massive deal means for Mets, suitors, all of MLB
features.desc: The two-time Cy Young winner is now baseball's highest-paid pitcher. Here's how Skubal's contract impacts the league.
body: Tarik Skubal is officially headed to the New York Mets on a record-setting $450 million contract.
Skubal pitched the final months of the 2026 MLB season with the Los Angeles Dodgers following a midseason blockbuster trade from Detroit, where he had previously spent his entire career.
After a free agency that earned interest from plenty of contenders, the superstar ace decided on the Mets on Sunday, ending his stay in L.A.

His nine-year, $450 million contract is now the largest in major league history for a pitcher. How does it change New York's outlook for 2027 — and beyond? Where should the Dodgers and other suitors turn now? And what does it mean for baseball ahead of the impending lockout?
Our MLB experts weigh in on Skubal's sport-altering deal.
Buster Olney: The contract numbers landed around where many in baseball believed they would, and it's not a surprise that it came down to the Mets.

They were desperate to sign him; owner Steve Cohen had negotiated a monster deal with Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, before; and Cohen is one of the few owners — maybe the only one — seemingly unconcerned with the potential financial ramifications for his team if baseball's financial system changes dramatically under a new collective bargaining agreement.
It was as if Captain Cohen shouted, "Damn the salary cap torpedoes, full speed ahead!"
Skubal gets paid, a little more than a week before the lockout deadline. But it appears more and more likely that 200-plus free agents will go without deals before the next CBA is forged.

features.headline: Tarik Skubal to Mets: Grading record $450 million contract
features.desc: New York has landed this offseason's most prized free agent. How did the Mets fare in handing out the mind-boggling contract?
body: Tarik Skubal is a New York Met — for $450 million over nine years!
It's not often that a two-time Cy Young winner still in his prime and regarded as one of the best starting pitchers in the game becomes available in free agency.

These are potential franchise-altering difference-makers, maybe a final piece needed to build a World Series champion. If you have an owner who wants to win and is willing to spend the money, you make it happen at any cost.
Steve Cohen and the New York Mets made it happen, landing Skubal for the largest total value contract ever for a pitcher, surpassing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's 10-year, $325 million deal with the Dodgers.
The 30-year-old left-hander needs no introduction: He won Cy Young Awards with the Detroit Tigers in 2024 and 2025, leading the American League in ERA and WAR both seasons.

Over the past three seasons, he's gone 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA, ranking first among all pitchers in FanGraphs WAR, second in Baseball-Reference WAR, second in strikeouts, second in ERA, third in strikeout rate, first in strikeout-to-walk ratio, second in lowest walk rate, fourth in batting average allowed, and 10th in home run rate.

Skubal's stuff matches the results: A 97 mph four-seamer (batters have hit.201 against it the past three seasons); a changeup that is considered one of the best in the game and helps him dominate right-handed batters as much as lefties; oh, and a sinker, slider and curveball.

He executes with precision and conviction. He's allowed no runs or one run in 44 of his 88 starts over the past three seasons. He should remain a Cy Young contender over much of the life of the contract if he stays healthy.

features.headline: Inside the gymnastics lore of Bengals star Ja'Marr Chase
features.desc: Ja'Marr Chase's skill set suggests formal gymnastics training, but the reality isn't quite that simple.
body: CINCINNATI — It was a move that looked so improbable that the majority of the 70,747 in attendance inside NRG Stadium didn't seem to process it in real time.
When the Cincinnati Bengals visited the Houston Texans in Week 2, quarterback Joe Burrow heaved a deep ball toward wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase ("F—- it, Ja'Marr's down there somewhere").
As Chase stumbled toward the near right corner of the end zone, he twisted his body, somehow located the ball to make the catch and then dragged both of his feet inbounds to complete a touchdown.

While the crowd in Houston reacted in disbelief as the replay on the videoboards confirmed it was a catch, TV announcer Kevin Harlan extolled the All-Pro receiver while watching the catch in slow motion.
"Oh, the contortion!," Harlan exclaimed. "The body control! The concentration!"
It was almost as if Harlan was talking about a gymnast. Instead, he was talking about a 6-foot, 205-pound dynamic route runner who is one of the best wide receivers in the NFL.
Over the years, Chase has spoken about how he took up gymnastics as a kid, once adding that it was something that never leaves his spirit.

Given how well he controls his body and can still backflip from a standstill position, it could seem as if those skills might have helped him become an All-Pro player. But with a bit more digging, the reality isn't that linear.

"In gymnastics, you got to stick the landing," Bengals wide receivers coach Troy Walters told ESPN. "And in football, the more times you stick the landing and not go to the ground and fall down, probably the more successful you're going to be.

features.headline: The Connor McDavid Scoring Tracker: Can the Oilers' superstar break 200 points?
features.desc: Follow along game by game as No. 97 looks to break a benchmark that only No. 99 has done in NHL history.
body: There have been only four occasions in NHL history when a player scored 200 or more points in a single season, and only one player has accomplished the feat: Wayne Gretzky.
The Great One scored 215 points in 1985-86, 212 in '81-82, 208 in '84-85 and 205 in '83-84. Mario Lemieux came closest to Gretzky, finishing the '88-89 season with 199.
Connor McDavid plays for the same Edmonton Oilers franchise that Gretzky did when he posted those totals, and his personal best total is 153, set in 2022-23.
There are cases for and against McDavid breaking the 200-point barrier this season, as his pace fluctuates on a game-by-game basis.
Follow along below to monitor his pace after every game, along with highlights of memorable moments along the way.

body: For some athletes, there's no such thing as a day off.
Baltimore Orioles legend Cal Ripken Jr. had perfect attendance during a 17-season stretch of his 21-year career, amounting to 2,632 games played without missing one.
